stories.title: Jensen Huang says 'honoured' to return as CEO if asked; Nvidia chairman says no plans to do so
stories.summary: Huang said he received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return
stories.title_zh: 黄仁勋称如受邀将"荣幸"回归CEO职位；Nvidia董事长表示无此计划
stories.content:
Huang said he received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return

NVIDIA on Tuesday (Nov 17) rejected Jensen Huang’s offer to return as CEO, putting to rest for now any possible reinstatement of the celebrated artificial intelligence billionaire and industry evangelist, despite pressure from Silicon Valley and US President Donald Trump’s support.

The embattled company’s board of directors “unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call before yielding to chief financial officer Colette Kress, who is running the company as a permanent replacement is sought.

The rejection caps a whirlwind few days triggered by Huang’s admission to extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman and suspected spy for the country, his stunning ouster and a surprising split in the Trump administration over the fate of the disgraced business leader.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a wholesale cleaning at Nvidia on Sunday, only for Trump to come out in support of Huang’s return the next day despite investigations into whether Nvidia had allowed AI chips banned from China to slip through the cracks because of the alleged spy at the center of the controversy.

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said in a social media post that if the board decided that his return was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and the country, he would be “honoured to answer these calls.” He acknowledged making “serious mistakes” in his personal life.

Santa Clara, California-based Nvidia did not respond to an earlier Associated Press request for comment on Huang’s statement.

## Company reports blowout financial results

The turmoil notwithstanding, Nvidia blew past Wall Street expectations for the third quarter, pulling in US$116 billion in revenue, double the level from a year ago. The company also posted net income of US$2.70 per share, beating estimates of US$2.48 per share.

Nvidia stock shot up 5.2 per cent in after-hours trading.

Referring to Huang’s replacement, Jones said, “We want to install the permanent CEO as quickly as possible, but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.”

Some tech industry figures, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, called for the reinstatement of Huang, a high-profile booster for the AI industry who oversaw Nvidia’s development as the key provider of chips driving advanced AI models.

Huang said he received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return.

A “Stand with Jensen” petition set up last week gathered momentum, gaining signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other Silicon Valley supporters.

In comments on Monday, Trump suggested that the ex-CEO could return, saying Huang “learned a big lesson” and that he “would certainly not mind” if he was reinstated.

The Chinese businesswoman whom Huang was seeing and who reportedly had links to Chinese intelligence was an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, a company being investigated by the US for allegedly violating U.S. export controls by illegally diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies.

## Huang faces questioning by Congress

Also on Tuesday, key House lawmakers said that Huang has voluntarily agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the company faces intensifying national scrutiny over sales of its advanced computer chips.

Huang will appear before congressional committees on Dec 1, followed by the company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, on Dec 2.

“The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips,” said a statement from the chairmen of three House committees with oversight of China and intelligence issues, referring to the People’s Republic of China.

In the statement detailing its August-to-October results, Nvidia said revenue in a key business segment – data centres – more than doubled to US$107.6 billion. It also projected that revenue for the current quarter running through January would hit US$130 billion, more than Wall Street had expected.

Nvidia’s advanced chips are in high demand because they’re essential for cloud computing and data centers that underpin the AI boom, but they face restrictions on their sale to China.

Meanwhile, Nvidia said it’s creating a new board committee to oversee national security and global trade compliance following the revelations about Huang. Trump said it was “good” that Nvidia had created the new committee.

“Yes, that’s a good idea. It’s a great company,” Trump said shortly after arriving Tuesday evening in the Philippine capital of Manila, where he participated in a photo opportunity with the leaders of Australia, India and Japan. “It’s a great idea.”

Nvidia later that day signalled it was already moving ahead without Huang.

“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating,” interim CEO Kress said at the end of the quarterly conference call with investors. “We’ve got this.” AP

stories.title_zh: NVIDIA动荡标志着AI交易轻松赚钱时代的终结
stories.content:
NEW YORK (Nov 17): Tumult at Nvidia spells the end of easy money for the AI sector and a funding squeeze for smaller, highly leveraged "neocloud" companies that have helped fuel the industry's rapid expansion.

In recent years, Nvidia's financial support has boosted infrastructure providers and other partners of the giant chip firm. Bond investors say the uncertainty over who might eventually succeed ousted chief executive officer Jensen Huang has raised questions about Nvidia's willingness to continue support through vendor financing, guarantees and other methods, hitting these firms' shares and bonds.

"It's fair to say that anyone who takes over is going to have a lower risk threshold than Jensen when it comes to Nvidia's balance sheet," said Loren Moran, a fixed income portfolio manager at Wellington Management. "There may just be a lot less credit availability toward weaker players."

Chief among the firms cast in an uncertain new light are the so-called neocloud firms such as CoreWeave and Nebius, cloud computing companies that acquire graphics processing units (GPUs) or electronic chips, renting out computing capacity to AI developers, start-ups, and large technology companies.

Last week, credit investors resumed their retreat from bonds exposed to Nvidia-related risk. Bonds in CoreWeave issued in June at a yield of 9.625% plunged in value, sending their yield to nearly 15%. The company's shares have lost 45% since the Nasdaq hit its latest record on Oct 6, even after the company said on its earnings conference call last week that it would be able to continue to finance its operations by doing things such as borrowing against its chips.

Nvidia is a shareholder and buyer of last resort for CoreWeave's unsold cloud capacity through April 2032 under a US$6.3 billion (RM25.8 billion) order.

Convertible bonds of Nebius, issued at a 4.5% yield in August, dropped to 70 US cents to the dollar last Friday, sending yields surging to more than 12%. Nebius rents out the computing power that AI firms need to train and run their models. Nvidia said in March it would invest US$2 billion in Nebius, representing an 8.3% stake in the company. Nebius stock is down 57% since Oct 6.

Many of these neocloud companies operate with smaller balance sheets while relying heavily on external financing to fund the enormous costs associated with acquiring GPUs and building data centres.

"Nvidia's contracts and existing guarantees should not change with Jensen Huang's departure," said Tony Trzcinka, an investment-grade portfolio manager at Impax Asset Management. "It's all about whether Jensen's successor would want to be as adventurous in going into all these different arrangements."

For Nvidia itself, some investors argued that a more conservative approach to balance sheet risk could be credit-positive. Wellington's Moran said she was concerned about the company's huge financial commitments across the AI space and believes a reduced appetite for risk could "clip some of that tail".

But a more cautious Nvidia could have different implications for the broader AI financing environment. It could, for instance, widen the disparity between investment-grade borrowers and lower-rated companies dependent on private credit, leveraged loans and high-yield debt markets. Companies relying on financing tied directly or indirectly to Nvidia may find future capital either harder to obtain or significantly more expensive, analysts said.

Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Microsoft appear best positioned to weather such a shift, investors say, given their strong balance sheets that can finance data centre construction on their own.

"Most of their AI spending comes from internal cash flow and debt markets," said Danny Zaid, a portfolio manager at TwentyFour Asset Management, and that is "unlikely going to change in the near term with the strong AI momentum expected to continue".

At the other end of the spectrum, investors have already been demanding greater compensation to finance data centre projects from lower-rated AI borrowers. "In a construction phase \[of a project\] where there is a high-yield name, you're going to have a materially higher cost of funding," said Trzcinka of Impax.

In Goldman Sachs' "Top of Mind" research note, Miriam Wheeler, the bank's global head of leveraged finance, said the pace of AI deals in the high-yield market has significantly slowed in recent weeks amid investor concerns over mounting supply and political uncertainty.

Wheeler said the market had expected roughly US$60 billion of issuance this fall, which had pressured spreads. But supply has dried up since late September, "with no new deals over the past month".

The slowdown suggests the easy financing conditions that have fueled AI-linked issuance are beginning to fade, analysts said.

"The uncertainty for the overall space means greater risk premiums expected by investors," said Zaid of TwentyFour Asset Management. "Expect dispersion to increase as investors evaluate credits on a case-by-case basis."

stories.title: Vertiv signs three-year Infineon pact to secure chips
stories.summary: The pact should help keep data centre power systems supplied as AI-driven demand pushes Vertiv to scale output and avoid chip shortages.
stories.title_zh: Vertiv与Infineon签署三年协议确保芯片供应
stories.content:
Wed, 18th Nov 2026 (Today)
Vertiv has signed a three-year strategic agreement with Infineon to secure supplies of power semiconductors. The deal covers silicon and silicon carbide components used across Vertiv's global power product portfolio.

The agreement builds on a relationship spanning decades and is designed to give Vertiv greater visibility over semiconductor supply as it increases production.

Power semiconductors are used to convert, manage and distribute electrical power within Vertiv's systems. They form part of the company's wider power product range, including its 800 VDC power systems for digital infrastructure.

Demand for that equipment has risen as data centre operators respond to changing computing loads linked to artificial intelligence. The agreement is intended to support continuity of supply and on-time delivery as those requirements grow.

### Supply focus

The arrangement also fits within Vertiv's broader multi-supplier approach to supply-chain management. That model is intended to strengthen resilience across its manufacturing operations while reducing the risk of disruption in a market where semiconductor availability remains a concern for industrial buyers.

Infineon's components are manufactured globally and will be integrated into Vertiv products sold worldwide. Those products serve data centres, communications networks, and commercial and industrial users.

Vertiv selected Infineon for its offering across insulated-gate bipolar transistor, silicon and silicon carbide technologies, as well as its manufacturing footprint and quality record. Under the new agreement, the two companies will also continue to align their technology and product roadmaps.

### AI demand

The tie-up reflects how suppliers to data centres are trying to secure critical components as operators invest in systems that can handle higher and more variable power loads. Semiconductor supply has become a strategic issue for equipment makers whose products operate in electricity-intensive computing environments.

Vertiv's next-generation 800 VDC systems are part of that shift. Higher-voltage direct current architectures are drawing attention as data centre operators and infrastructure providers look for ways to improve efficiency and power distribution in facilities designed for AI-related workloads.

Frieda He, chief procurement officer at Vertiv, linked the agreement to those changing requirements.

“The rapid evolution of AI is reshaping the power requirements of the data centre, and our customers need infrastructure partners who can anticipate what comes next,” said Frieda He, chief procurement officer at Vertiv.

“This agreement strengthens our ability to deliver for customers today while supporting the next generation of power architectures required for AI and other critical applications. By aligning our technology roadmaps with Infineon and securing access to critical power semiconductors, we are taking another proactive step that enables our customers to scale with confidence,” she said.

For Infineon, the deal underlines the importance of industrial and infrastructure demand for both silicon and silicon carbide devices. These components are increasingly used in large electrical systems where efficiency, thermal performance and power density matter.

The agreement gives Infineon a committed route into a major buyer serving global digital infrastructure markets. It also shows how semiconductor makers are using longer-term supply relationships to anchor demand in sectors beyond consumer electronics.

Andreas Weisl, executive vice president and chief sales officer for industrial & infrastructure at Infineon, said the partnership reflected shared priorities between the two companies.

“The agreement with Vertiv reflects our shared commitment to supporting the evolving requirements of critical power infrastructure,” said Andreas Weisl, executive vice president and chief sales officer for industrial & infrastructure at Infineon.

“Through our comprehensive portfolio and manufacturing capabilities, we can provide Vertiv with the advanced power semiconductor technologies needed to support its continued innovation and growth,” he said.

stories.title: Google expands TPU line-up with two new AI systems
stories.summary: The new chips aim to win regulated customers and agent-heavy workloads as Google Cloud races rivals on speed, memory and data controls.
stories.title_zh: Google推出两款新AI系统扩展TPU产品线
stories.content:
Google has expanded its eighth-generation Tensor Processing Unit line-up with TPU 8i Max and TPU 8tx, bringing its TPU releases this year to four systems.

The new systems target different AI workloads in Google Cloud. TPU 8tx is aimed at secure and confidential inference, while TPU 8i Max is designed for workloads that need large context windows and greater compute density within the same rack footprint.

Google said the launch reflects broader demand from customers using AI for model training, inference and autonomous agents. It added that TPUs are now used by nearly 100 customers, including frontier laboratories, trading firms, retailers and universities.

### New systems

TPU 8tx is built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and is paired with fifth-generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts. Google said it is intended for regulated enterprises and government users that want to run models and agents alongside sensitive data.

According to Google, TPU 8tx protects data and model weights while they are in use through hardware-level confidential computing. It also uses the same Boardfly network introduced for lower-latency reasoning workloads, delivering up to half the latency of TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty, the company said.

The set-up is intended to let customers run inference and smaller-scale training on the same system. Organisations can fine-tune models with private data, distil larger models into smaller ones and train agents through reinforcement learning without moving sensitive data across separate clusters, Google said.

TPU 8i Max is designed to address what Google described as the memory bottleneck in AI systems. It combines two low-latency TPU 8i chips into a single package, doubling compute, SRAM and high-bandwidth memory bandwidth compared with TPU 8i, according to the company.

Google said the result is a system for workloads in which multiple agents work across large code bases or extended video inputs. It added that the design fits twice the silicon into the existing rack footprint, allowing data centres to deploy more compute per square foot and per watt.

### Broader portfolio

The launch expands Google's eighth-generation TPU family to four products: TPU 8t for large-scale training, TPU 8i for lower-latency reasoning, TPU 8tx for confidential computing and TPU 8i Max for high-context workloads.

Google said this system-level approach allows it to respond more quickly to changing customer requirements than waiting for a full new chip generation. Rather than redesigning silicon each time, it modifies the surrounding compute, networking, storage and packaging to create more specialised systems.

"With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models' massive context windows," Google said.

"In addition, some highly regulated customers are asking for specialized encryption capabilities for unique workloads."

### Software push

Alongside the hardware additions, Google outlined a broader effort to make TPUs easier for developers and cloud customers to use. It said PyTorch code and Hugging Face models now run natively on TPUs through the open-source TorchTPU project, while TPU back ends are available for open-source inference engines including vLLM and SGLang.

Google also said a TPU agent suite in preview can plug into coding tools to automate onboarding, diagnose bottlenecks and tune kernels. For production use, its open-source XLA Serving Engine allows customers to train models in Python and serve them in a C++ runtime across TPUs, GPUs and CPUs.

Other software updates include Agent Compute Engine, which suspends and resumes idle agent sessions to reduce infrastructure costs, and TPU Sync, which manages model state across high-bandwidth memory, host memory, storage and network resources. Google said TPU Sync can reduce key-value transfer latency and time to first token by more than 90%.

It also pointed to the general availability of Cloud Pathways on Google Kubernetes Engine, extending distributed runtime tools used internally for Gemini to Google Cloud customers. In a separate update, Google said GKE dynamic slicing now lets users reconfigure TPU topologies on demand, cutting job start-up times by up to five times and improving fault recovery by up to 4.5 times.

### Competitive backdrop

The expanded TPU range comes as cloud groups and chip suppliers compete to meet demand for AI computing infrastructure, particularly for workloads that need lower latency, larger memory footprints and stronger data controls. Google said the broader range reflects increasingly specialised demand as customers move from traditional model training to inference-heavy and agent-based applications.

Google also said it has been using AI tools from Google DeepMind in its chip design process, including AlphaChip reinforcement learning systems and Gemini-based design tools. According to the company, those tools have helped cut parts of chip layout work from weeks to hours.

"Shipping four TPU systems and a unified, open software stack in a single year only happens when silicon architects, networking engineers, compiler teams and Google DeepMind researchers build side by side," Google said.

stories.title: Nvidia doubles quarterly earnings, raises forecast, 'does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO'
stories.summary: Nvidia reported quarterly earnings that doubled year-over-year and raised its forward revenue guidance, underscoring sustained demand for its AI accelerators despite mounting trade restrictions. The company also clarified governance matters by stating it does not plan to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as CEO, a formulation suggesting board-level succession planning discussions may have surfaced amid his prolonged tenure.
stories.why_it_matters: The earnings trajectory confirms that US chip controls have not yet dented Nvidia's core revenue engine, though the China sales halt creates a medium-term growth gap the company must fill through non-China markets and new product cycles. The unusual CEO clarification hints at investor pressure around leadership transition risk at a critical inflection point for the $3 trillion chipmaker.
stories.title_zh: NVIDIA季度收益翻倍，上调预测，"不打算恢复Jensen的CEO职位"
stories.summary_zh: Nvidia季度earnings同比翻倍，并上调了forward revenue guidance，突显尽管贸易限制不断增加，对其AI accelerators的需求依然持续。该公司还澄清了治理问题，表示不打算重新任命创始人Jensen Huang为CEO，这一表述暗示在其长期任期内可能出现了board-level succession planning讨论。
stories.why_zh: earnings轨迹证实美国芯片管制尚未削弱Nvidia的核心收入引擎，尽管停止对华销售造成了该公司必须通过非中国市场和新产品周期填补的中期增长缺口。这一不寻常的CEO澄清暗示，在这家3万亿美元chipmaker的关键拐点，投资者对leadership transition risk施加了压力。
stories.content:
Nvidia reported revenue up 103 percent over last year, beating expectations at $115.84 billion.

However, the company reiterated that it has no plans to bring back founder Jensen Huang, who left this month amid numerous affairs. This quarter was the last with Huang at the helm.

The company reported earnings of $2.68 per share, also above Wall Street expectations.

Data center revenue was $107.6bn, up 110 percent year-over-year. Edge computing revenue hit $8.2bn, up 42 percent. Net profit hit $65.3bn, up 105 percent.

Crucially, amid broader market uncertainty, interim CEO Colette Kress raised guidance by five percent, saying that Nvidia now expects 75 percent growth.

The former CEO said that it was "business as usual at Nvidia.”

She added: “Our leadership has stood up so strongly over the last week to support both what we are doing here at earnings, but also supporting all of our different employees around the world.

“Remember, we have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap. And I think that’s important from a business perspective.”

Unresolved questions still remain over whether Nvidia will continue to backstop deals with its customers, fund startups buying GPUs, and make large financial commitments to keep the AI economy going.

The company said it is "not assuming any data center compute revenue from China in our outlook," but it faces investigations into its role in selling chips to Singapore that ended up in China. The company has denied any wrongdoing.

Nvidia has faced mounting calls to reinstate Jensen Huang, who was fired after admitting an affair with an executive accused of funneling chips into China. Huang also had multiple affairs with Nvidia staffers.

Board chair Harvey Jones pushed back on those calls, saying in the earnings call that Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

stories.title: University of Osaka launches SEAFOOD platform to link Octopus supercomputer with quantum processors
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka have developed a hybrid computing infrastructure to link its Osaka University Compute and sTOrage Platform Urging open Science (OCTOPUS) supercomputer with…
stories.title_zh: 大阪大学推出SEAFOOD平台，将Octopus超级计算机与quantum processor连接
stories.content:
Researchers at the University of Osaka have developed a hybrid computing infrastructure to link its Osaka University Compute and sTOrage Platform Urging open Science (OCTOPUS) supercomputer with Japanese-made superconducting quantum processors.

The platform, dubbed SEAFOOD (Supercomputing Entangled by Ambitious Fusion of OQTOPUS and OCTOPUS at D3C), is expected to be operational in December 2026 and represents the first integration of a Japanese-developed quantum computer with a supercomputer at a standalone academic institution in the country.

No details about the quantum processors were provided, but the university said they were provided by the RIKEN Center for Quantum Computing.

According to the university, the SEAFOOD platform partitions workloads across three-layer stacks, allowing each processor to undertake the calculations best suited to its hardware design. In 2027, up to ten research teams at the University of Osaka will receive trial access to the program before the platform is made available to broad external access via Japan’s JHPC-quantum initiative.

JHPC-quantum is a research project that supports the development of a hybrid computing platform to integrate quantum processors with classical high-performance computing infrastructure.

The project was supported by Japan’s JST Moonshot Goal 6, MEXT Q-LEAP, JST COI-NEXT, CSTI SIP, and NEDO’s Post-5G quantum-supercomputer hybrid platform program.

OCTOPUS was developed by NEC Corporation. The system has a theoretical computational performance of 2.293 petaflops, with around 140 computing nodes of the "NEC LX201Ein-1," each equipped with two sixth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors and large-capacity storage. According to NEC, it provides around 1.5x the performance of the previous system at the D3 Center.

The University of Osaka D3 Center, according to its website, provides "large-scale computer systems as a national joint-use facility where scientists and researchers can perform computation and information processing accompanied by academic research and education."

The center also operates the MDX II and SQUID clusters and the ONION aggregation platform.

stories.title: Macquarie Data Centres eyes 200MW campus in Sydney, Australia
stories.summary: Macquarie Data Centres is planning a 200MW campus development in Sydney, Australia, that would significantly expand the company's footprint in the Asia-Pacific region's most mature data center market. The proposed capacity reflects confidence in sustained demand from Australian government, financial services, and hyperscale cloud customers despite increasing competition from global operators.
stories.why_it_matters: The 200MW scale positions Macquarie to compete directly with global hyperscale self-builds and established colocation leaders for enterprise and cloud tenancy, intensifying supply competition in a market where land and power constraints already favor incumbent developers. Australian data center pricing and contract structures face downward pressure as new capacity enters, while Macquarie's infrastructure investment mandate may enable more patient capital deployment than publicly traded competitors.
stories.title_zh: Macquarie Data Centres计划在澳大利亚悉尼建设200MW园区
stories.summary_zh: Macquarie Data Centres正在规划在澳大利亚悉尼建设一个200MW campus，这将显著扩大该公司在亚太地区最成熟data center市场的footprint。拟议的capacity反映了对澳大利亚政府、金融服务和hyperscale cloud客户持续需求的信心，尽管来自全球运营商的竞争日益激烈。
stories.why_zh: 200MW的规模使Macquarie能够直接与全球hyperscale self-builds和established colocation领导者竞争enterprise和cloud tenancy，在土地和电力约束已经有利于incumbent developers的市场中加剧供应竞争。随着新capacity进入，澳大利亚data center定价和合同结构面临下行压力，而Macquarie的infrastructure investment mandate可能使其比上市竞争对手进行更耐心的资本部署。
stories.content:
Australian operator Macquarie Data Centres is planning a new campus in Sydney.

In a SEARS application with the New South Wales Government, the company has filed to develop the Macquarie Engineering and Technology Campus.

Located at 2 Alma Road in the Macquarie Park area of the city of Ryde, the company aims to develop a 200MW, 42,015 sqm (452,245 sq ft) campus on the site, demolishing the existing office buildings.

Some AU$2 billion (US$1.35bn) is set to be invested in the project. The development could comprise six stories. Timelines for development were not shared.

The site totals around 3.4 hectares and is currently made up of two existing buildings. The land was recently split off from the neighboring plot at 66 Talavera Road, which features an office building built in 2015 and occupied by AstraZeneca.

Founded in 1992, Macquarie Technology Group currently has two buildings in operation (IC2 and IC3 East) and one more in development (IC3 Super West) around Macquarie Park, totaling a combined 65MW across 30,000 sqm (322,915 sq ft). The company topped out its 47MW IC3 Super West facility in December 2025. It has another facility (IC1) in Sydney’s central business district.

In July 2025, Macquarie said it was set to buy more land in Sydney for a new data center, but had provided few details beyond the fact that it was aiming to develop 150MW of new capacity.

The company also has two bunker data centers in Canberra.

stories.title: Rakuten Mobile, JTower pair to expand infra sharing to more than 1,000 sites in Japan
stories.summary: Japanese carrier Rakuten Mobile and JTower have outlined plans to expand the usage of infrastructure sharing across the country.
stories.title_zh: Rakuten Mobile与JTower合作，将日本基础设施共享扩展至1000多个站点
stories.content:
Japanese carrier Rakuten Mobile and JTower have outlined plans to expand the usage of infrastructure sharing across the country.

The companies announced last week that the expansion of their existing partnership will expand the infrastructure sharing to more than 1,000 indoor and outdoor sites in more than 500 municipalities across the country by the end of March 2027.

Rakuten Mobile said that the agreement will enable the carrier to strengthen its network footprint more efficiently.

The company, which established itself as a mobile network operator in 2018, before launching services as an MNO in October 2019, recently surpassed 11 million subscribers across Japan.

Rakuten Mobile added that it's also advancing the use of base stations on utility poles and accelerating the deployment of its own base stations by reforming its construction processes, including bringing certain operations in-house.

This has seen the company leverage its RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) to automatically adjust base station antenna angles and output, ensuring both coverage and optimal network performance, as well as improving capital expenditure efficiency. The RIC uses AI to manage and control the RAN.

To support the infrastructure sharing project, JTower has set up a dedicated division for Rakuten Mobile’s network development projects. The division will handle equipment installation negotiations, design and construction coordination, plus launch preparations as a single process, as it aims to deploy sites more quickly.

When it comes to indoor network deployments, Rakuten Mobile notes that it will prioritize its network equipment at large facilities where heavy traffic is expected. These will be selected from the approximately 900 facilities JTower already operates.

"The companies are further accelerating development through a multi-pronged approach. This includes synchronizing with JTower’s ongoing 4G equipment modernization projects, conducted in partnership with other mobile carriers, and proactively installing shared infrastructure in newly constructed facilities," said Rakuten Mobile in its announcement.

Rakuten has already started providing services using JTower’s infrastructure sharing solutions at large facilities where heavy traffic is expected at sites including Akasaka Trust Tower (Minato-ku, Tokyo), Glion Arena Kobe (Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture), Aeon Mall Kobe Kita (Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture) and Imperial Hotel Kyoto (Kyoto, Kyoto Prefecture). More deployments will follow, added the company.

Founded in 2012, JTower has more than 7,000 telecom towers across Japan, offering infrastructure sharing to Japan's network carriers. The company was acquired by DigitalBridge in 2024.

stories.title: GIC and Saudi Telecom compete on Pure DC minority stake bid
stories.summary: Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC and Saudi Telecom Company are competing to acquire a minority equity stake in Pure DC, a data center development platform with assets across European and potentially Asian markets. The competitive bidding process highlights converging investment interests between Gulf and Asian state-backed capital in infrastructure assets that generate stable, long-denominated cash flows.
stories.why_it_matters: The GIC versus STC contest illustrates how data center platforms have become geopolitically contested assets where investment decisions carry implicit alliance signaling. For Pure DC, choosing between Asian and Middle Eastern capital partners determines future geographic expansion priorities and customer access, with the outcome potentially influencing whether the platform prioritizes ASEAN growth or Gulf-European corridor development.
stories.title_zh: GIC 与 Saudi Telecom 竞购 Pure DC 少数股权
stories.summary_zh: 新加坡主权财富基金GIC和Saudi Telecom Company正在竞争收购Pure DC的minority equity stake，Pure DC是一家在欧州和潜在亚洲市场拥有资产的data center development platform。竞争性竞标过程突显了海湾和亚洲国家支持资本在产生稳定、长期现金流infrastructure assets中的converging investment interests。
stories.why_zh: GIC与STC的竞争说明data center platforms如何成为geopolitically contested assets，投资决策带有implicit alliance signaling。对Pure DC而言，在亚洲和中东资本伙伴之间选择决定了未来的geographic expansion priorities和客户准入，其结果可能影响该平台是优先发展东盟增长还是Gulf-European corridor development。
stories.content:
Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC and Saudi Telecom Company are reportedly bidding for a stake in UK-based Pure Data Centres (Pure DC).

Bloomberg reports that Pure DC owner Oaktree Capital Management was looking to bring in a minority investor to fund the developer’s expansion.

The report said GIC had joined with Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) for its bid.

According to Bloomberg’s sources, Oaktree is seeking an $8 billion valuation for Pure DC. *DCD* has reached out to the involved parties for confirmation and further information.

Earlier this month, Pure DC secured $1.9 billion in new financing to support its data center buildout. The latest announcement puts the company’s year-to-date secured financing at more than $6bn.

Backed by Oaktree, Pure DC claims to have more than 1GW of IT capacity in operation or development across Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. The company aims to triple this capacity and position itself as a leader in data centers in Europe and the Middle East.

GIC was established by the government of Singapore in 1981. It has invested in a range of data center operations in recent years, including Vantage’s EMEA data center platform, multiple Equinix xScale hyperscale data centers, US firm EdgeCore, and Czech digital infrastructure firm CETIN Group.

In August, GIC and Macquarie Asset Management formed a strategic partnership with Anthropic to develop, operate, and lease data center infrastructure at scale to Anthropic.

Saudi Telecom Company is a Saudi state-owned telecoms company. It is actively expanding its presence in the Middle East and North Africa and has 25 data centers operational and under construction.

stories.title: China's LineShine retains supercomputing crown as both Top500 and Green500 lists remain largely unchanged
stories.summary: The November 2026 edition of the Top500 list of most powerful supercomputers has seen no changes to the top ten.
stories.title_zh: 中国 LineShine 保持 supercomputing 冠军地位，Top500 和 Green500 榜单基本不变
stories.content:
The November 2026 edition of the Top500 list of most powerful supercomputers has seen no changes to the top ten.

According to the Top500, the November list saw new system turnover fall to a historic low, with only 27 new system entrants – “the lowest number ever recorded by a wide margin.”

The highest-ranking new system was the 342.6 petaflops Hangang, installed at the KITSI Supercomputing Center in South Korea, which ranked 12th. The supercomputer is powered by Nvidia Grace CPUs alongside GH200 Superchips.

The Green500 list of most energy-efficient supercomputers also saw an unchanged top ten. However, while the traditional Top500 has four US entrants, alongside systems from China and Japan, in its top ten, the Green500 top ten is almost entirely dominated by European systems, with three housed in France, three in Germany, and one each in the United Kingdom and Poland.

The lack of new entrants is not an indication that the performance of systems has stopped improving, the Top500 said, rather that most of the improvement growth is coming from additions and upgrades towards the top of the list, rather than wholesale replacements of leading supercomputers.

Consequently, for the second edition in a row, the Top500 was topped by China’s LineShine. The system boasts 2.198 exaflops of HPL performance, taking first place from America's El Capitan supercomputer in June 2026.

LineShine is housed at the National Supercomputing Centre in Shenzhen and consists of Chinese-designed chips and networking gear, including semi-custom 304-core LX2 processors based on the Armv9 instruction set architecture running at 1.55GHz. The LX2 appears to have been co-designed with China's National Supercomputing Center and Huawei, with 40,960 chips deployed across 92 cabinets. It has a total of 13,789,440 cores.

The full HPL top ten was:

1. LineShine, National Supercomputer Center, Shenzhen, China. 2.198 exaflops.
2. El Capitan, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, United States. 1.809 exaflops.
3. Frontier, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, United States. 1.353 exaflops.
4. Aurora, Argonne National Laboratory, United States. 1.012 exaflops.
5. JUPITER Booster, Jülich Supercomputing Centre, Germany. 1.000 exaflops.
6. HPC7, Eni, Italy. 571.5 petaflops.
7. Eagle, Microsoft, United States. 561.2 petaflops.
8. HPC6, Eni, Italy. 477.9 petaflops.
9. Supercomputer Fugaku, RIKEN Center for Computational Science, Japan. 442.01 petaflops.
10. Alps, Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS), Switzerland. 434.9 petaflops.

stories.title: Digital Realty launches liquid cooling lab in Singapore
stories.summary: Digital Realty has opened a liquid cooling laboratory at its Singapore facility to validate and optimize thermal management technologies for high-density AI workloads. The lab enables customers to test direct-to-chip and immersion cooling configurations before deployment, addressing the escalating power densities of GPU clusters that exceed traditional air conditioning capabilities.
stories.why_it_matters: Singapore's tropical climate and constrained land availability make liquid cooling adoption economically essential rather than optional for sustaining the city-state's competitiveness as an AI hub. Digital Realty's facility investment pressures competing colocation providers to offer equivalent testing capabilities or risk losing hyperscale tenants with thermal specifications that cannot be met by legacy infrastructure.
stories.title_zh: Digital Realty 在新加坡推出 liquid cooling lab
stories.summary_zh: Digital Realty在其新加坡设施开设了liquid cooling lab，用于验证和优化high-density AI工作负载的thermal management技术。该实验室使客户能够在部署前测试direct-to-chip和immersion cooling配置，解决超过传统空调能力的GPU clusters escalating power densities问题。
stories.why_zh: 新加坡的热带气候和有限的土地可用性使liquid cooling adoption成为维持其作为AI hub竞争力的经济必需，而非可选。Digital Realty的设施投资迫使竞争的colocation提供商提供同等的测试能力，否则可能失去thermal specifications无法由legacy infrastructure满足的hyperscale租户。
stories.content:
The company last week announced the opening of its second Digital Realty Innovation Lab (DRIL) in Asia Pacific, located at its four-story, 90,500 sq ft (8,400 sqm) SIN11 facility at Digital Loyang 1 (3 Loyang Way) in Loyang.

The lab aims to provide enterprises with a real-world colocation environment inside a live data center to test, validate, and optimize integrated, multi-vendor AI infrastructure solutions before deploying at scale.

The lab offers the ability to test liquid-cooled racks supporting cabinet densities of 150kW and above.

"Enterprises deploying AI want to understand how different components and technologies can perform together before committing to infrastructure at scale," said Chris Sharp, Digital Realty CTO. "The DRIL will provide a production-grade testing environment where customers can work with leading technology partners and our engineering teams to validate AI, high-performance computing and hybrid cloud architectures under real-world conditions. By testing performance, fit, and readiness before deployment, enterprises globally and across Asia Pacific will be able to scale with confidence and achieve more impactful outcomes with AI."

The company currently has liquid cooling labs at its facilities in London, Virginia, Tokyo, and São Paulo.

Further DRIL locations, including in Johannesburg, are planned for late 2026.

stories.title: Nvidia board sets up committee to oversee export control compliance
stories.summary: Nvidia's board of directors created a dedicated National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee with permanent standing status to supervise compliance with US export regulations and manage global trade risks. The committee's establishment at board level rather than within management structures reflects elevated governance expectations for semiconductor companies operating under intensifying US enforcement regimes.
stories.why_it_matters: Board-level export control oversight becomes a template for peer semiconductor and cloud infrastructure firms, with institutional investors and regulators likely to mandate similar structures as a condition of capital market access. The committee's permanence signals that trade compliance has transitioned from a transactional legal function to a sustained strategic risk requiring continuous director attention and potential liability exposure.
stories.title_zh: Nvidia董事会设立委员会监督export control合规
stories.summary_zh: Nvidia董事会设立了一个具有永久地位的National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee，负责监督美国export regulations compliance并管理global trade risks。该委员会在board level而非管理层结构中设立，反映了在加强的美国执法制度下运营的半导体公司面临的elevated governance expectations。
stories.why_zh: Board-level export control oversight成为同行半导体和cloud infrastructure公司的模板，机构投资者和监管机构可能将类似结构作为资本市场准入的条件。委员会的永久性表明，贸易合规已从transactional legal function转变为需要持续董事关注和潜在liability exposure的持续战略风险。
stories.content:
The Nvidia Board of Directors has established a new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management as the US prepares to crackdown on illicit exports and remote access to American technology.

The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, as it has been named according to a press release, will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and will oversee Nvidia’s efforts to enhance its internal National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team. The committee will also work closely with independent third-party experts in law, national security, and global trade compliance.

“NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security. As the world’s leading advanced computing company, NVIDIA has both a responsibility and an opportunity to lead the industry in addressing these challenges,” said Harvey Jones, Chairman of Nvidia’s Board of Directors.

Nvidia added that the decision to establish this committee reflects the Board’s commitment to enhancing engagement with relevant government stakeholders to demonstrate the highest standards of governance and oversight.

“We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation,” added Jones.

The committee will also include Nvidia directors Stephen Neal and John Dabiri. It will meet quarterly at the very least where management and the executive team will be included. The National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report to the committee and interim CEO Colette Kress on day-to-day operations.

The Nvidia announcement comes a day after the US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released an interim final rule requiring licenses for exports of advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. The rule aims to stop chips from being diverted through these countries to restricted destinations, and to curb remote access to advanced computing power based on US technology.

stories.title: Banks pause US$480 million chip loan tied to China's ByteDance
stories.summary: Financial institutions have halted a $480 million loan facility intended to fund chip purchases linked to ByteDance, the Chinese parent company of TikTok, after the US introduced licensing requirements for data center operators in Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The suspension reflects heightened lender caution as geopolitical risk now directly intersects with semiconductor financing structures in Southeast Asia.
stories.why_it_matters: Project finance for Chinese-affiliated data center ventures in ASEAN is becoming structurally precarious as US extraterritorial controls force banks to reprice sovereign and counterparty risk. Lenders will increasingly demand political risk insurance or sovereign guarantees for chip-backed facilities, potentially raising capital costs for Chinese hyperscalers and redirecting investment flows toward non-sanctioned ownership structures.

stories.summary_zh: 在美国对新加坡、泰国、印尼和马来西亚的data center运营商引入购买美国芯片的许可证要求后，金融机构暂停了一笔4.8亿美元、用于购买与中国ByteDance相关芯片的贷款。此次暂停反映了随着地缘政治风险直接与东南亚半导体融资结构交叉，贷款方谨慎情绪的加剧。
stories.why_zh: 随着美国extraterritorial controls迫使银行重新定价主权和交易对手风险，中国在东盟关联的data center项目融资正变得结构性不稳定。贷款方将越来越多地要求芯片支持设施的政治风险保险或主权担保，可能提高中国hyperscalers的资本成本，并将投资流向重新导向非受制裁的所有权结构。
stories.content:
The US announced a rule requiring data centre operators in countries including Singapore and Malaysia to get a license to buy advanced AI chips

BANKERS have frozen work on a US$480 million loan that would have funded advanced Nvidia chips for use by China’s ByteDance, according to people familiar with the matter.

After the US placed its latest curbs on access to AI chips, bankers at five lenders evaluating the deal have had internal discussions about pulling out or not joining the loan amid fears of violating the new restrictions, the people said.

Singapore-based neocloud Aolani Cloud recently began inviting banks to join the loan, which would fund the purchase of GPUs for a data centre in Malaysia.

But on Monday, the US announced a rule requiring data centre operators in countries including Singapore and Malaysia to get a license to buy advanced AI chips.

The step is aimed at curbing Chinese companies’ remote access to such technology, which is how TikTok parent ByteDance would use the Nvidia GPUs.

The pause in work on the loan illustrates how the Trump administration’s surprise move has caught many dealmakers in Asia off-guard.

Across the region, lenders scrambled on Tuesday to work out what the new regulations would mean for billions of AI debt in the pipeline and deals that have already been done.

“We have spent significant time with our banking and financing partners to assess and anticipate regulatory risk ahead of this recent new ruling,” a spokesperson for Aolani said in response to questions about the loan being paused. “We are pro-actively working with regulators and our financing partners to ensure the project delivery goes ahead in full compliance with the new ruling.”

DBS Group, which is the mandated lead arranger and book-runner on the deal, declined to comment.

It’s not yet clear how exactly the license approval process will work, and which firms will be required to apply for them. That’s prompted a barrage of questions from potential lenders, one of the people said.

It’s unlikely that there would be progress on funding the Aolani deal until bankers can fully evaluate the new rule, the people said.

Internally, some bankers have described the facility as dead given the risks banks could incur if it was found to violate the new US rule, they said. BLOOMBERG

stories.title: Immersion cooling adoption faces cost, cultural barriers
stories.summary: Immersion cooling offers high energy efficiency and zero water use, but its adoption remains rare in data centers. High upfront costs and industry resistance to change are significant barriers to widespread deployment.
stories.title_zh: 浸没式冷却采用面临成本与文化障碍
stories.content:
Immersion cooling, a technique for cooling IT equipment by immersing it in liquid, offers high energy efficiency and requires no water.Despite these benefits, it has not become a mainstream cooling strategy among major data center operators, with most headlines focusing on pilots and demonstrations.Direct-to-chip cooling, another liquid cooling method, is projected for rapid growth, unlike immersion cooling.
### Key Barriers to Adoption

Immersion cooling systems are significantly more expensive to install than alternatives. Implementing an immersion cooling system costs approximately $1 million per MW of IT load, compared to $650,000 for direct-to-chip cooling.While immersion cooling can reduce operational costs over time through lower energy use and improved thermal efficiency, these long-term benefits often do not outweigh the higher upfront capital expenditure.The data center industry's resistance to change also poses a cultural barrier. Immersion cooling disrupts traditional data center design, maintenance procedures, monitoring practices, and technician training.Direct-to-chip cooling, by contrast, requires less disruptive changes, allowing operators to retain more of the conventional server and rack paradigm, which facilitates easier incremental adoption.
### Future Outlook

Future adoption of immersion cooling will depend on how data center cooling demands evolve, especially with power-hungry workloads like AI training. Denser compute environments could strengthen the case for technologies capable of handling extreme thermal loads.However, if the AI boom plateaus, immersion cooling may remain largely experimental. Reduced public and regulatory pressure on water consumption also lessens the urgency for water-free solutions.Concerns about data centers' impact on power grids could encourage more operators to consider immersion cooling for improved power usage effectiveness (PUE). However, cooling is a secondary factor in overall data center power consumption.

# Immersion cooling adoption faces cost, cultural barriers

Immersion cooling offers high energy efficiency and zero water use, but its adoption remains rare in data centers. High upfront costs and industry resistance to change are significant barriers to widespread deployment.

- Published On Nov 17, 2026 at 04:50 PM IST

## Highlights

- Immersion cooling offers energy efficiency and zero water use for data centers.
- Upfront costs for immersion systems are higher, at $1 million per MW of IT load.
- Industry inertia and operational disruption hinder widespread adoption despite long-term savings.
- Future AI workloads and power grid pressures could drive increased interest in immersion cooling.

stories.title: China taps US AI models to train home-grown rivals as chip curbs bite
stories.summary: Beijing is encouraging the use of distillation to make AI easier to deploy across the manufacturing sector
stories.title_zh: 随着芯片限制收紧，中国利用美国AI模型训练本土竞争对手
stories.content:
Beijing is encouraging the use of distillation to make AI easier to deploy across the manufacturing sector

\[BEIJING\] Chinese entities are adopting increasingly sophisticated ways to use output from leading American artificial intelligence models to train domestic rivals, documents show, as China aims to broaden its AI strategy and offset tightening US curbs on its access to chips.

A Reuters review of more than 300 Chinese academic papers, patents, corporate disclosures, recruitment notices and government documents reveals how the practice – known as distillation – has expanded beyond academic experiments into mainstream industrial use in China.

The records describe Chinese researchers using US models to produce answers to questions, build computer code and find solutions to difficult problems, with Chinese companies then developing software to automate the process and specialist workers preparing material for training smaller domestic models.

The documents also show that Beijing is encouraging distillation to make AI cheaper and easier to deploy across China’s powerful manufacturing sector.

Distillation is not illegal and is prevalent in other parts of the world.

While the process cannot reproduce a leading model’s full capabilities or eliminate the need for advanced computing power, it can help developers preserve selected skills in smaller systems that cost less to operate, potentially reducing their reliance on American technology.

China’s broadening use of distillation could undercut the effectiveness of US curbs on the sale of advanced chips to China, as its developers can build AI capabilities by drawing on those of their American rivals.

Washington said on Monday (Nov 16) it would further restrict China’s access to such chips from companies like Nvidia.

Distillation is also a source of friction between the world’s two biggest economies ahead of the Nov 18 to 19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, where US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are expected to meet.

US authorities publicly accused Chinese companies in September of aggressive, targeted distillation of American AI models on an industrial scale.

And at meetings in Chengdu in July, US Commerce Department officials raised concerns with Chinese regulators about developers collecting output from leading American AI models, warning that some activities could amount to intellectual property (IP) theft, three people familiar with the discussions said.

Chinese officials defended distillation as a standard AI-development technique and said they were open to acting where the conduct constituted IP theft, but made no concrete commitments, according to a US official familiar with the previously unreported exchange.

The US Commerce Department and China’s Cyberspace Administration did not respond to requests for comment.

## From American answers to Chinese models

Distillation involves a powerful “teacher” model generating answers or demonstrating how to complete tasks, which developers use to train a smaller “student” system.

For Chinese developers facing constraints on computing power, the attraction is in making one expensive query do repeated work, according to a former Alibaba Group engineer who spoke on condition of anonymity.

An American model can generate the answer to a difficult question once, allowing a Chinese team to retain useful examples and train a local system around them.

In a November 2024 paper, Shanghai Jiao Tong University researchers described selecting about 5,000 answers from OpenAI’s o1 model, translating them using GPT-4o mini and assembling 10,750 bilingual training examples to further train Alibaba’s Qwen2.5-72B model.

The researchers also cautioned that excessive reliance on distillation could stifle original innovation, leaving developers dependent on breakthroughs made by more advanced model providers.

The project illustrated how American model output can become reusable data, allowing developers to improve domestic systems without repeatedly consulting the original provider.

Alibaba researchers described a more systematic approach in an April 2025 paper, using OpenAI’s GPT-4 and GPT-4o to generate training material in languages other than Chinese, then refining and scoring responses before training smaller Qwen models.

In a February 2026 paper, researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Chinese food delivery company Meituan described using GPT-4o to generate plans for coordinating AI agents working together on programming problems, helping train a smaller model to organise such tasks.

Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Alibaba and Meituan did not respond to requests for comment.

## A growing geopolitical dispute

Among leading American AI companies, OpenAI’s terms restrict using its output to develop competing models, subject to exceptions, while Anthropic similarly restricts training competing systems without permission.

A US official familiar with the July Chengdu regulatory discussions said Washington believes industrial-scale distillation is the main reason Chinese AI models have narrowed the gap with their American rivals.

Two people familiar with Chinese developers’ operations disputed that assessment, saying distillation was only one factor alongside advances in engineering, algorithms, data and model design.

Chinese government documents do not instruct companies to distil American models but encourage distillation as part of Beijing’s push to spread AI across the world’s second-largest economy.

A national AI+Manufacturing policy package published by eight Chinese government agencies in January includes guidance supporting model training, fine-tuning and distillation for industrial applications.

Shanghai and Shenzhen have also encouraged techniques to reduce computing requirements.

The policies reflect Beijing’s ambition to deploy smaller, cheaper AI systems across industries.

Concerned by distillation’s growing geopolitical sensitivities, Chinese AI developers have in recent months asked Beijing’s industry regulator for guidance on the boundaries between ordinary use of foreign models and organised collection of output for training, according to one person familiar with the discussions.

China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to a request for comment. REUTERS

stories.title: Core Scientific to exit Bitcoin mining by end of 2026 as it grows AI colo business
stories.summary: Cryptomining and AI infrastructure firm Core Scientific has announced it expects to exit the Bitcoin mining industry by the end of 2026, as it looks to pivot its business towards high-density…
stories.title_zh: Core Scientific将于2026年底前退出Bitcoin挖矿，同步扩张AI colocation业务
stories.content:
Cryptomining and AI infrastructure firm Core Scientific has announced it expects to exit the Bitcoin mining industry by the end of 2026, as it looks to pivot its business towards high-density colocation for AI workloads.

“We expect to complete our exit from bitcoin mining by year-end,” CEO Adam Sullivan said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call on November 5.

Chief financial officer Jim Nygaard said the company had nearly 50 percent fewer miners online at the end of September than at the end of 2025.

Core Scientific expects to complete the wind-down in Q4 and enter 2027 operating solely as a high-density colocation provider.

The company’s accompanying 10-Q filing also disclosed equipment sales, listing mining, electrical, and high-performance computing (HPC) equipment as held for sale during Q3, having initially earmarked mining and electrical equipment for disposal in Q2.

Some assets were sold during the current quarter, leaving the remaining equipment held for sale carrying a value of $29.7 million at September 30. The company expects the sales to be completed within one year of the assets’ initial classification.

Revenue from mining Bitcoin for its own account fell to $12.3 million in Q3, from $57.4 million a year earlier. Revenue from hosting third-party miners declined to $5.2 million from $8.7 million. Together, the two mining businesses generated $17.4 million, compared to $66.2 million in Q3 2025.

Core Scientific also sold 3,374 Bitcoin for $286.8 million during the first nine months of 2026 to fund capital expenditure and other cash requirements. It held 32 Bitcoin, worth $2.7 million, at the end of September, compared with 2,537 Bitcoin at the end of 2025.

The Q3 results showed colocation increasingly dominating the business. Total revenue rose to $232.9 million from $81.1 million a year earlier, with colocation contributing $215.4 million, compared with $15 million in Q3 2025. Colocation accounted for approximately 92.5 percent of quarterly revenue.

Adjusted EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) reached $133.6 million, up from $41.1 million in Q2 and $6.5 million in Q3 2025. Core Scientific reported net income of $1.18 billion, compared with a $144 million loss a year earlier, primarily driven by a non-cash gain from the revaluation of warrants.

Capital expenditure, including land and development rights acquisitions, totalled $985.1 million. The company ended September with $803.9 million in cash and cash equivalents.

Core Scientific was billing for 485MW of colocation capacity at the end of September, up from 395MW at the end of June. Its earnings presentation shows 590MW contracted to CoreWeave across five campuses, with full delivery expected in early 2027.

Beyond CoreWeave, the company has 530MW contracted under its partnership with AMD, comprising direct AMD leases and leases with an AMD-backed neocloud. The capacity spans Pecos and Hunt County in Texas; Dalton, Georgia; Muskogee, Oklahoma; and Auburn, Alabama. Initial deliveries are expected in the first half of 2027, with the full programme due for completion by the end of 2028.

In August, Core Scientific completed its acquisition of Polaris DS for around $444 million, adding a former cryptomining site adjacent to its Muskogee campus. The deal provided approximately 40 acres and 440MW of grid-connected power capacity as part of plans to expand the campus to 1.5GW of gross power.
